rubric.judge: Direct review by the Codex assistant; no judge model or metric LLM.
rubric.ragas.context_precision: RAGAS-style average precision evaluated separately for each retrieval-query leg, then averaged across legs. Reset rank at each query and de-duplicate identical filename/text chunks within that leg, so a corrective leg is not treated as if it were appended below the initial ranking. The hand-labeled expected_source documents define relevance. Use 0 for a leg with no expected-source context.
rubric.ragas.context_recall: Fraction of hand-labeled expected_source documents represented anywhere in the retrieval trace.
rubric.ragas.faithfulness: Fraction of factual claims in the actual answer supported by the retrieval trace. Use 1 for an answer containing no unsupported factual claims and 0 for a wrong abstention on an answerable case.
rubric.deepeval.answer_correctness: Fraction of required expected-answer facts stated correctly, with unsupported or contradictory additions reducing the score.
rubric.deepeval.hallucination_rate: Fraction of actual-answer factual claims that are unsupported by or contradict the retrieved evidence. Lower is better.
rubric.deepeval.citation_accuracy: Fraction of factual claims whose adjacent filename citations point to passages that support those claims. Missing required citations score 0.
rubric.custom.abstention_accuracy: Binary: 1 when an unanswerable case abstains, or an adversarial case refuses, corrects the false premise, or flags and ignores an injection as expected; else 0.

Document filename: 02_aws_deployment_runbook.docx Agentic CRAG AWS Deployment Runbook Operations Guide - Demo Corpus Deployment Shape The demo deployment uses one Ubuntu EC2 instance. FastAPI listens on 127.0.0.1:8000 and Streamlit listens on 127.0.0.1:8501. Nginx listens publicly on port 80. Requests to /api/ are proxied to FastAPI. Requests to / are proxied to Streamlit. The intended storage root on EC2 is /opt/agentic-crag/data. The environment file should live at /opt/agentic-crag/.env. The repository should be cloned to /opt/agentic-crag/app. The systemd services expect the virtual environment at /opt/agentic-crag/app/venv. Security Group Rules Inbound SSH on port 22 should be restricted to the developer current public IPv4 address using a /32 source rule. Inbound HTTP on port 80 may be opened to 0.0.0.0/0 for a temporary demo, but the instance should be stopped or locked down after use. The EC2 instance should not expose FastAPI port 8000 or Streamlit port 8501 directly to the public internet. Nginx should be the public entry point. For a longer-lived deployment, add HTTPS, a domain name, and authentication before sharing the application broadly. Setup Commands The recommended initial package command is: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y python3 python3-venv nginx git. A small instance may need a swap file. The demo runbook uses a 2 GB swap file at /swapfile to reduce dependency installation failures. After cloning the repository, run bash deploy/setup_ec2.sh from /opt/agentic-crag/app for repeatable setup. After editing /opt/agentic-crag/.env, restart the application services with sudo systemctl restart agentic-crag-api agentic-crag-ui. Health Checks The backend direct health check is curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health. The Nginx-routed health check is curl http://127.0.0.1/api/health.

Document filename: 04_release_notes.docx Agentic CRAG Release Notes Versions 2.2, 2.3, and 2.4 - Demo Corpus Version 2.2 Version 2.2 introduced saved collections and a registry file for local metadata. The registry stores folder_path, folder_name, and a list of document filenames and types. Version 2.2 used simple chat responses that returned only answer text. Source snippets were not yet exposed to the UI. Version 2.2 supported PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads. Legacy XLS files were allowed by extension but were not reliable because the parser expected openpyxl-compatible files. Version 2.3 Version 2.3 added AWS hybrid deployment documentation. The deployment used EC2, systemd, and Nginx. Version 2.3 clarified that public demo documents should be used because retrieved excerpts are sent to Groq in hybrid mode. Version 2.3 added a default local storage recommendation of .agentic_crag_data for Windows development and /opt/agentic-crag/data for EC2 deployment. Version 2.4 Version 2.4 added structured source reporting to chat responses. The chat response now includes an answer field and a sources list. Version 2.4 added a retrieval debugging endpoint named POST /retrieve. The endpoint returns source snippets without calling the language model. Version 2.4 updated Streamlit to display source snippets in a Sources expander under assistant responses. Version 2.4 added regression coverage for source formatting behavior. Version 2.4 did not add reranking or hybrid BM25 search because the deployment target was a small EC2 instance and the goal was minimal code. Compatibility Notes Collections built before a chunking or embedding change should be rebuilt to ensure retrieval uses the current settings. Changing from Groq to a local Ollama model can alter answer style, even when the same base model family is used. Groq model name llama-3.1-8b-instant refers to a hosted serving configuration. The closest local Ollama model family is llama3.1:8b, but outputs may differ.

sources.text: Document filename: 04_release_notes.docx Agentic CRAG Release Notes Versions 2.2, 2.3, and 2.4 - Demo Corpus Version 2.2 Version 2.2 introduced saved collections and a registry file for local metadata. The registry stores folder_path, folder_name, and a list of document filenames and types. Version 2.2 used simple chat responses that returned only answer text. Source snippets were not yet exposed to the UI. Version 2.2 supported PDF, DOCX, and XLSX uploads. Legacy XLS files were allowed by extension but were not reliable because the parser expected openpyxl-compatible files. Version 2.3 Version 2.3 added AWS hybrid deployment documentation. The deployment used EC2, systemd, and Nginx. Version 2.3 clarified that public demo documents should be used because retrieved excerpts are sent to Groq in hybrid mode. Version 2.3 added a default local storage recommendation of .agentic_crag_data for Windows development and /opt/agentic-crag/data for EC2 deployment. Version 2.4 Version 2.4 added structured source reporting to chat responses. The chat response now includes an answer field and a sources list. Version 2.4 added a retrieval debugging endpoint named POST /retrieve. The endpoint returns source snippets without calling the language model. Version 2.4 updated Streamlit to display source snippets in a Sources expander under assistant responses. Version 2.4 added regression coverage for source formatting behavior. Version 2.4 did not add reranking or hybrid BM25 search because the deployment target was a small EC2 instance and the goal was minimal code. Compatibility Notes Collections built before a chunking or embedding change should be rebuilt to ensure retrieval uses the current settings. Changing from Groq to a local Ollama model can alter answer style, even when the same base model family is used. Groq model name llama-3.1-8b-instant refers to a hosted serving configuration. The closest local Ollama model family is llama3.1:8b, but outputs may differ.

Document filename: 03_rag_evaluation_plan.docx Agentic CRAG RAG Evaluation Plan Quality and Stress Testing - Demo Corpus Evaluation Goals The evaluation plan tests whether the RAG system retrieves the right evidence, answers faithfully, cites useful sources, and refuses unsupported questions. The system should be tested with exact fact questions, numeric spreadsheet questions, multi-document comparison questions, ambiguous questions, and answer-not-present questions. A good result is not only a fluent answer. The retrieved source snippet must support the answer. Primary Metrics Recall@5 measures whether the expected source appears in the top five retrieved chunks. Citation accuracy measures whether the source shown under the answer actually supports the answer. Answer correctness measures whether the final response matches the expected answer. Faithfulness measures whether the final response is fully grounded in retrieved context. Abstention accuracy measures whether the system refuses questions whose answers are absent from the documents. Latency measures indexing time, retrieval time, and full chat response time. Stress Test Questions Question A: What does FR-006 require? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: a retrieval-only endpoint for debugging top retrieved chunks without spending LLM tokens. Question B: What path stores data on EC2? Expected source: AWS deployment runbook. Expected answer: /opt/agentic-crag/data. Question C: What is the Q3 Groq API budget? Expected source: budget workbook. Expected answer: 75 dollars. Question D: Which risk has the highest probability score? Expected source: risk workbook. Expected answer: R-004, missing source citations, probability 0.70. Question E: Is authentication included in the current release? Expected source: product requirements document. Expected answer: no, authentication is not included. Question F: What is the company payroll for 2026? Expected answer: not present in the documents, so the system should abstain. Pass Criteria For a recruiter demo, the system should achieve at least 80 percent answer correctness on the curated test questions. For source transparency, at least 80 percent of correct answers should show a supporting source snippet. For answer-not-present questions, the system should avoid inventing facts at least 90 percent of the time.
